description: Free commission calculator: sales or real estate commission at a flat or tiered rate, your take-home after a split and fees, and sales needed for a goal.

jsonld.name: Commission Calculator
jsonld.description: Commission calculator for flat or marginal tiered rates with brokerage split, per-deal fees and sales volume needed for an income goal.

acceptedAnswer.text: Split arrangements vary widely by brokerage, industry and experience — 70/30 is a commonly cited example, but actual splits range broadly and are often negotiable, especially as your production increases.

mainEntity.name: Does this calculator handle tiered commission structures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose "Tiered" and set up to three bands. Each rate applies only to the portion of the sale inside its band, the way marginal tax brackets work.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate commission on a sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the sale amount by the commission rate — for example, $50,000 × 5% = $2,500. Then multiply by your split percentage and subtract any per-deal fees to get your take-home.

mainEntity.name: Is commission calculated before or after tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before tax. The figures here are gross commission and take-home after split and fees, before income tax or self-employment tax.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate real estate commission?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the sale price by the commission rate, then apply your split. A $400,000 sale at 3% is $12,000 gross, or $8,400 for you on a 70/30 split.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate commission with a quota?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pay the base rate on sales up to the quota and the higher rate above it. With a $100,000 quota, 5% to quota and 8% above, a $150,000 month pays $9,000.
A fixed salary plus a percentage of sales. A $50,000 base plus 4% on $600,000 of sales is $74,000.

mainEntity.name: How much does eBay take from a sale?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most US categories the eBay selling fees page lists 13.6% of the total sale up to $7,500 and 2.35% above, plus $0.30 per order of $10 or less or $0.40 above. On a $100 sale that is $14.00. Check eBay for current rates and your category.

mainEntity.name: How much does PayPal charge to receive a payment?

acceptedAnswer.text: PayPal's US business fees page lists 3.49% plus $0.49 per checkout transaction, which is $3.98 on a $100 sale. Rates vary by payment type.

mainEntity.name: How much should I charge to cover PayPal fees?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the amount you want to receive plus $0.49 by 0.9651. To receive $100 charge about $104.12.

mainEntity.name: Is commission taxed differently from regular pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is taxable income, but withholding can use a flat supplemental rate or the aggregate method, so it may look different on a paycheck. Check IRS Publication 15 or ask payroll.

mainEntity.name: What is a typical commission split?

acceptedAnswer.text: It varies widely by brokerage and experience. A 70/30 split is a common example, and splits often improve as you sell more.
